verdict: valid conditional endpoint bound if actual rounded al_pert and addition are enclosed
derivation: At captured FP64 profile source computes al_pert_native from basic tensor operations, alt_native=fl(al_pert_native+alb_stored), and returns both cast to ph output dtype; FP64 output cast preserves values.

Define δadd=alt_native-(al_pert_native+alb_stored); ideal al_pert*=alpha*−alb*. Then al_pert_native−al_pert*=(alt_native−alpha*)+(alb*−alb_stored)−δadd; triangle gives E_alpert<=E_composed_alpha+E_upstream_alb+E_add.

Existing EOS domain I uses outward rounded operations for muts, denominator, numerator and pre-add neg/div; expose that exact pre-add interval, then add captured alb under exact rational arithmetic to bound the exact native addition input. Do not substitute the widened ideal-alb tube for the stored-alb rounded-operation tube.

If every exact pre-round sum has absolute value strictly below 8 and operation is finite IEEE binary64 RN, one full ulp 2^-50 is conservative, including near crossing 8; no assumption on sign. Capture FP64 output type; guard no unexpected fusion/reassociation or alternative arithmetic semantics.

For reported endpoint L-infinity bounds, 1.6996994953743442e-15 + 1.245771593971007e-15 + 2^-50 < 4e-15 when adding the actual binary64 upper bounds exactly/outward. Per-level bounds may tighten only if paired with corresponding per-level registered upper bounds.
conditions: All tube input/shape/level/coefficient provenance must be verified and native source operation order and rounding semantics assumed; cross-endpoint input ranges must contain the observed endpoint.
Use binary64 hex encodings/Fraction.from_float for existing upper bounds and exact rational aggregation, not inward decimal reinterpretation or nearest-only floating accumulation.
Proves endpoint component al_pert error conditional on exact stored inputs and collision-qualified reconstructed theta; not full RHS, scaled residual, forcing or descent.
validation: read-only source/math review; no execution of MPFR, model or tests
